---
# render_farm_nodes: GPU render nodes for the render farm workshop

- name: Show the target region
  ansible.builtin.debug:
    msg: "Deploying {{ guid }} to {{ aws_region }}"

- name: Launch the render nodes
  amazon.aws.ec2_instance:
    region: "{{ aws_region }}"
    image_id: ami-0c7d41e9b25f83a16    # RHEL 9 render image
    instance_type: "{{ render_farm_node_type }}"
    count: "{{ render_farm_node_count }}"
    key_name: "{{ guid }}-key"
    vpc_subnet_id: "{{ render_farm_subnet_id }}"
    tags:
      guid: "{{ guid }}"
      lab_role: render-node
    wait: true
  register: r_render_nodes

- name: Wait for the render nodes to pass status checks
  amazon.aws.ec2_instance_info:
    region: "{{ aws_region }}"
    instance_ids: "{{ r_render_nodes.instance_ids }}"
  register: r_render_info
  until: r_render_info.instances | map(attribute='state.name') | unique == ['running']
  retries: 30
  delay: 10

answer:
Job 418627 (GUID qpl3n) failed in "Launch the render nodes": RunInstances returned InvalidAMIID.NotFound, "The image id '[ami-0c7d41e9b25f83a16]' does not exist".

Regions: the failed job 418627 deployed to eu-central-1 ("Deploying qpl3n to eu-central-1"). The successful job 418655 (GUID h8sxt) deployed to us-east-1 and launched two g5.2xlarge nodes from the very same ami-0c7d41e9b25f83a16 in us-east-1b.

Why one worked and the other did not: AMI IDs are region-specific. agnosticd/agnosticd-v2:ansible/roles/render_farm_nodes/tasks/main.yml:11 hard-codes image_id: ami-0c7d41e9b25f83a16, an image that exists only in us-east-1, while the task passes region: "{{ aws_region }}". In us-east-1 the ID resolves; in eu-central-1 there is no image with that ID, so AWS says it does not exist. The AMI was not deregistered: job 418655 launched it successfully more than two hours after the failure.

Fix: stop hard-coding the ID. Resolve the image per region, for example with amazon.aws.ec2_ami_info filtering on the image name and owner in aws_region, or keep a per-region map of AMI IDs (and copy the image into each supported region) and select it with aws_region.
